answer: Sybil resistance is a cellar acoustic gate. An applicant reserves one alcove at a mapped building's structural nadir and hangs a uniquely serialled timber panel, cut from one tagged bole, as the back wall. A registrar later arrives unannounced and speaks a one-time whisper against the panel; a contact mic on the deed-tagged edge records the live grain-borne arrival, matched to the bole's ring print and alcove log. A reused panel, a shared alcove, or a playback counts as one farm. Minting N aliases costs N reserved alcoves, N unique panels, and N surprise visits, not a copied recording.
